title: Raw local inverse through common stages and both Karoubi layers
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Index by its small directed poset of finite intermediate fields [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal A_E,\mathcal B_E$ be additive categories [def-weil-additive-category] with additive transition functors [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor] $U_{M/E},V_{M/E}$, identity transitions literally identities, and specified natural associators with identity unit cases and the pentagon equation. Form the finite-stage categories $\mathcal A_E^+=\Kar(\mathcal A_E)$, $\mathcal B_E^+=\Kar(\mathcal B_E)$ with extended transitions, their common-stage pair categories $P_A,P_B$ of [lem-sbc-coherent-pair-functor-descent], and their outer Karoubi envelopes [def-weil-karoubi-envelope]. No idempotent completeness of the raw categories is assumed.

Let $F_E,G_E:\mathcal A_E\to\mathcal B_E$ be additive functors, with specified natural comparison isomorphisms $b^F_{M/E}:V_{M/E}F_E\xrightarrow{\sim}F_MU_{M/E}$ and $b^G$ satisfying the unit and tower equations of [lem-sbc-coherent-pair-functor-descent]. Let $\eta_E:F_E\Rightarrow G_E$ be natural transformations satisfying
$$\eta_MU_{M/E}\circ b^F_{M/E}=b^G_{M/E}\circ V_{M/E}\eta_E.$$
Use the Karoubi extensions $F_E^+(A,p)=(F_EA,F_E(p))$, $G_E^+$ likewise, $\eta^+_{E,(A,p)}=G_E(p)\eta_{E,A}F_E(p)$, the extended transitions $U^+_{M/E}(A,p)=(U_{M/E}A,U_{M/E}(p))$ and $V^+_{M/E}$ likewise, and the extended comparisons $b^{F,+}_{M/E,(A,p)}=F_M(U_{M/E}(p))\,b^F_{M/E,A}\,V_{M/E}(F_E(p))$ with inverse $V_{M/E}(F_E(p))\,(b^F_{M/E,A})^{-1}F_M(U_{M/E}(p))$, and $b^{G,+}$ likewise; these satisfy the unit, tower and compatibility equations above. Use the descended functors $\overline F,\overline G:P_A\to P_B$ and transformation $\overline\eta$, followed by their outer Karoubi extensions $\widehat F,\widehat G,\widehat\eta$.

Fix $A\in\mathcal A_E$ such that $a=\eta_{E,A}$ has a two-sided inverse $v$ in the raw category $\mathcal B_E$, and let $p:A\to A$ be any idempotent. Put $Q=(E,(A,p))\in P_A$ and $w=F_E(p)vG_E(p)$. Then $\widehat\eta$ is invertible on every object $(Q,q)\in\Kar(P_A)$, with $q$ any pair-category idempotent, and its inverse is precisely the outer Karoubi arrow with underlying pair morphism
$$\overline F(q)\,[E,w]\,\overline G(q).$$
The corresponding forward arrow is $\overline G(q)[E,G_E(p)aF_E(p)]\overline F(q)$. Their composites are $\overline F(q)$ and $\overline G(q)$, the actual Karoubi identities. In particular this applies with both $p$ and $q$ identities, using only the raw inverse $v$.

For every $M\supseteq E$, $\eta_{M,U_{M/E}A}$ is invertible with inverse
$$v_M=b^F_{M/E,A}\,V_{M/E}(v)\,(b^G_{M/E,A})^{-1}.$$
On the identity-projector object $Q_0=(E,(A,1))$, the same descended component is represented at $M$ by
$$[M,(b^G_{M/E,A})^{-1}\eta_{M,U_{M/E}A}b^F_{M/E,A}],$$
and its inverse by $[M,(b^F_{M/E,A})^{-1}v_Mb^G_{M/E,A}]$, with the displayed raw arrows included by identity idempotents at stage $M$. These classes are independent of $M$, including $M=E$, and of the chosen raw inverse. If $t:(Q,q)\xrightarrow{\sim}R$ is any isomorphism in $\Kar(P_A)$, then
$$\widehat\eta_R=\widehat G(t)\widehat\eta_{(Q,q)}\widehat F(t)^{-1}$$
has inverse $\widehat F(t)(\widehat\eta_{(Q,q)})^{-1}\widehat G(t)^{-1}$. Thus isomorphic presentations give the same component after the specified endpoint identifications. Invertibility is required only at the displayed raw object, not at every object of every stage.

proof.text: We use right-to-left composition throughout. The Karoubi morphism condition in [def-weil-karoubi-envelope] is equivalent to the two equations du=u=ue: multiply u=due by d or e, and conversely combine them. Thus F^+(u)=F(u) preserves the morphism condition, compositions and identities (the identity at (A,p) is p). For a natural transformation x:H⇒J put x_p=J(p)x_AH(p). Naturality gives J(p)x_A=x_AH(p), so x_p is a Karoubi arrow. For u:(A,p)→(B,r), J(u)x_p=x_rH(u) follows by inserting u=ru=up into ordinary naturality. For composable transformations x:H⇒J and y:J⇒K, y_p x_p=K(p)y_AJ(p)x_AH(p)=K(p)y_Ax_AH(p)=(yx)_p, and (1_H)_p=H(p). These calculations verify extension on functors and transformations without any splitting of p.

proof.text: Apply step 1 to every transition and associator as well as F_E,G_E,b^F,b^G and η_E. If x is a natural isomorphism with inverse y, their restricted composites are the respective projectors by the composition calculation, so the inverse of x_p is y_p. This gives exactly the displayed restricted b and inverse formulas. Extension commutes with whiskering: a functor H sends the restriction dxe to H(d)H(x)H(e), and evaluation at a functor image uses that image's projector. Hence restricting each side of each given unit, pentagon, tower and η-compatibility equation gives the corresponding equation for the extended data; internal projectors disappear by step 1's composition calculation. In a unit equation the restricted identity is the projector, which is the actual identity in the Karoubi category. Finally these extensions are additive in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor] since they send arrows by additive functors and restriction is multiplication by fixed projectors. The Karoubi categories are additive in the sense of [def-weil-additive-category]: Hom groups are closed under addition, (0,0) is zero and (A,p)⊕(B,r)=(A⊕B,p⊕r), with inclusions and projections restricted by p,r; their biproduct equations reduce to p²=p,r²=r. Thus the hypotheses of additive pair descent hold.

proof.text: Write e=F_E(p), d=G_E(p), a=η_{E,A}. Naturality at p gives da=ae. Since va=1 and av=1, multiplication by v on both sides gives vd=ev. Let c=dae and w=evd. They satisfy dce=c and ewd=w, so they are Karoubi arrows by [def-weil-karoubi-envelope]. Their composites are wc=evda e=eva e=e and cw=daevd=davd=d (using da=ae, vd=ev and idempotence). Consequently the restricted component c has exactly the claimed inverse w, even when neither projector splits in the raw category.

Therefore kg=kg(hk)=k(gh)k=k(hf)k=fk. Set H=ghf and K=fkg. The equations gHf=H and fKg=K show these are outer Karoubi arrows by [def-weil-karoubi-envelope]. Now KH=fkghf=fkhf=f and HK=ghfk g=ghkg=g. These are precisely the outer identities. Substituting h=[E,G_E(p)aF_E(p)] and k=[E,w] gives both formulas of the item. Setting p and q equal to their respective identities yields the identity-projector case.

proof.text: For M⊇E abbreviate b=b^F_{M/E,A}, c=b^G_{M/E,A}, and a_M=η_{M,U_{M/E}A}. The assumed compatibility is a_M b=c V_{M/E}(a), hence a_M=c V_{M/E}(a)b⁻¹. Define v_M=b V_{M/E}(v)c⁻¹. Functoriality gives V(v)V(a)=1 and V(a)V(v)=1. Consequently v_M a_M=b V(v)V(a)b⁻¹=1 and a_M v_M=c V(a)V(v)c⁻¹=1. This proves the claimed raw inverse at the transported raw object using invertibility only at A.

proof.text: For Q_0 the endpoints over M are V_{M/E}F_E(A) and V_{M/E}G_E(A), with identity inner projectors. The identities c⁻¹a_M b=V_{M/E}(a) and b⁻¹v_M c=V_{M/E}(v) follow from step 7. The representative equivalence in [lem-sbc-coherent-pair-functor-descent] identifies [M,V_{M/E}(a)] with [E,a] and [M,V_{M/E}(v)] with [E,v]: in its transport formula the associators a^B_{M,E,E} are identities because the last two fields agree. Thus the displayed conjugated arrows at M represent exactly the original component and inverse. For M=E all b and V are identities. For two overfields M,N the same argument identifies both representatives with the class at E (or transport them to a common overfield in the directed index). No literal equality of different endpoint presentations is asserted.

proof.text: If v' is another raw two-sided inverse, then v'=v'(av)=(v'a)v=v. Thus every displayed expression in v is independent of the raw inverse. More generally, any two inverses of h in a category coincide by the same calculation. In particular the representatives and both restricted inverses constructed above have no auxiliary inverse choice.

proof.text: Let X=(Q,q) and t:X≅R. The outer natural transformation supplied by [lem-sbc-coherent-pair-functor-descent] satisfies widehat η_R widehat F(t)=widehat G(t) widehat η_X. Composing with widehat F(t)⁻¹ gives widehat η_R=widehat G(t) widehat η_X widehat F(t)⁻¹. By step 6 its proposed inverse is widehat F(t) K widehat G(t)⁻¹. Multiplying the forward formula by this arrow in either order cancels the two functor images of t and uses KH=1_(widehat F X), HK=1_(widehat G X), giving the identities at widehat F R and widehat G R. This proves presentation independence with exactly the specified endpoint identifications, including any two choices of presentation isomorphism since each conjugation equals the same component widehat η_R.
